question.leadin: At the Battles of Issus and Gaugamela, Alexander the Great defeated forces from this empire.
question.text: Name this empire, which was ruled for some periods by Achaemenids, Safavids, and Afshars. Rulers of this empire included Cyrus the Great and Xerxes (ZERK-seez) the Great.
question.clue: One ruler of this empire famously ordered the ocean to be whipped.

swap.leadin: This ruler founded the Achaemenid [ah-KEE-men-id] Empire, which successfully grew by supporting local rulers as satraps and respecting local customs.
swap.text: Name this "Great" Persian ruler of the sixth century BCE who ended the Babylonian Captivity.
swap.clue: This victor of the Battle of Thymbra passed the Edict of Restoration, which granted the Jews religious tolerance, ending the Babylonian Captivity.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the SAVAK secret police force.
question.text: SAVAK was active in this country until its 1979 revolution, which saw the overthrow of its Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi. More than 50 Americans were held hostage in this country's city of Tehran.
question.answerHtml: Iran [or Islamic Republic of Iran or Jomhuri-ye Eslami-ye Iran; accept Iranian Revolution]
question.clue: This country created a literacy corps as part of its White Revolution.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the role of the pythia in Ancient Greece.
swap.text: The second Persian invasion of Greece was led by this monarch, the son of Darius I. While victorious at Thermopylae, his armies were defeated at Platea after they burned Athens.
swap.clue: This king's forces were decisively defeated at the Battle of Plataea (plut-AY-uh), after which Athens founded the Delian League.

question.leadin: Answer the following about civilizations that relied on horse archers.
question.text: Retreating horse archers would turn around to shoot arrows at the enemy in a "shot" named for this empire. This Persian empire between that of the Seleucids and the Sassanids used horse archers in their defeat of Crassus at the Battle of Carrhae.
question.answerHtml: Parthian Empire [accept Arsacid dynasty or empire; accept Parthian shot]
question.clue: At one battle, a general of this empire ordered his soldiers to cover their horses with cloth, thereby disguising the gleam of their armor.

swap.text: This Persian dynasty that succeeded the Parthians successfully besieged Constantinople in 626 CᐧE. Its first leader was Ardashir I.
swap.clue: Its last great ruler was deposed by Bahram, but with the help of Emperor Maurice regained the throne.

question.leadin: This man named 16 cities after his father, Antiochus.
question.text: Name this general who served under a famous Macedonian king during his Asian campaigns. He was also the first ruler of a namesake empire, the easternmost of the Macedonian successor states.
question.clue: He dispatched the ambassador Megasthenes on expeditions to the east, resulting in the production of theIndika.

swap.leadin: This empire was the last to have Zoroastrianism as a state religion.
swap.text: Name this empire founded by Ardashir I in 224 CE after defeating the Parthians at the Battle of Hormozdgan ["hor-moz-jan"]. Ardashir's son and successor, Shapur I, led this empire to its greatest extent later in the 3rd century CE.
swap.answerHtml: Sassanid Empire [or Neo-Persian Empire or the Second Persian Empire; accept Empire of the Iranians or Eranshahr; accept “Sassanian” in place of Sassanid; prompt on Persian alone]
swap.clue: This empire was defeated at Qadisiyyah at the hands of Umar's general, Khalid ibn al-Walid.

question.text: By dethroning his grandfather Astyages, Cyrus ended this empire, which was led from Ecbatana. Under Cyaxares, this empire took part in the conquest of Neo-Assyria.
question.clue: As a result of a battle at the Halys River, that waterway was declared its border with Lydia.

swap.text: Important to both the Medes and Persians were this priestly class which accomplished feats of prophecy, dream-interpretation, and sorcery later named for them.
swap.clue: Darius' rise to power is described in the Bisitun inscription, which claims that Gaumata, one of these people, pretended to be Smerdis, the brother of Cambyses II. These people, who in Sasanian times were led by a chief figure called the mowbed, are described by Herodotus as one of six Median tribes.

question.leadin: A ruler with this name had the Lakhmid king Al Nu'man III executed.
question.text: Give this name of a Sassanid shahanshah who then annexed the Lakhmid kingdom. An earlier shahanshah of this name went to war with Justinian after his allies raided the Lakhmids, who were then Sassanid vassals.
question.answerHtml: Khosrau [accept Khosrau I, Khosrau II, Khosrau Anushirawan, Khosrau the Just, or Chosroes]
question.clue: The second Sassanid ruler with this name held a truce with the Byzantine Empire because of his friendship with the Emperor Maurice, which lasted until Maurice was killed. The first began an "Eternal Peace" because of a bribe from Justinian, which lasted until that ruler got bored.

swap.leadin: One account says this ruler died while fighting Queen Tomyris and her Massagetae people.
swap.text: Name this ruler, whose son and successor was Cambyses II. He defeated the Babylonians at the battle of Opis and his Edict of Restoration ended the Israelites' Babylonian captivity.
swap.answerHtml: Cyrus II [accept Cyrus the Great or Cyrus the Elder]
swap.clue: This man defeated Nabonidus at the Battle of the Opis and bested Croesus at the Battle of Thymbra to conquer the Lydian Empire.

question.leadin: A widely rejected theory links the language of this ancient kingdom to South India's Dravidian language family.
question.text: Name this kingdom in modern Western Iran whose king, Shutruk-Nahhunte, took the stelae ("STEE-lee") of the Babylonian kings Naram-Sin and Hammurabi back to his capital of Susa during a 12th-century BC invasion of the Kassite Dynasty.
question.clue: The "Lament for Ur" describes a conquest by these people, whose Shutrukid dynasty later defeated the Kassites and looted the stele bearing the Code of Hammurabi from Babylon.

swap.text: The last Median ruler, Astyages, was overthrown by this grandson of his, who founded the Achaemenid Empire. He also allowed the Jews to return home after he conquered Babylon, and proclaimed an early charter of rights.
swap.answer: Cyrus the Great or Cyrus II
swap.clue: Indeed, he did overthrow Astyages in a rebellion against the Medes, and his Edict of Restoration gave the Jews permission to return to their homeland.

question.text: An image of the false Smerdis kneeling before Darius the Great can be found on this rock inscription in Kermanshah Province. Henry Rawlinson was the first to translate the writing on this rock relief.
question.answerHtml: Behistun Inscription [accept the Bisutun Inscription; or the Bisotun Inscription; or the Bagastana Inscription; or the Bisitun Inscription]
question.clue: This document justifies the position of the ruler who ordered it created by claiming that he saved the kingdom from the possibly fictional usurper Gaumata.

swap.leadin: The Jewish Babylonian form of this language is often found on incantation bowls.
swap.text: Name this language whose Syriac and Mandaic forms were also used at the time of the writing of the Babylonian Talmud. This language was spoken by Jesus.
swap.clue: Demons found in the Ginza Rabba were repelled using ceramic bowls with incantations in this language.

question.text: An "archaeological complex" named for Bactria and this region was home to Gonur Depe ("go-NOOR deh-PEH"), where Harappan seals have been found. A much later mention of this region's name appears in the Behistun Inscription, which records the rebellion of Frada there.
question.answerHtml: Margiana [or Marguš or Margush or Margiane or Marv; accept Bactria-Margiana Archaeological Complex; accept Frāda of Margiana]

swap.text: According to classical sources, the Kingdom of Urartu's capital of Tushpa fell to these people under Cyaxares in 590 BC. Herodotus described seven concentric walls surrounding this kingdom's mountain capital of Ecbatana.
swap.answerHtml: Medes [or the Median Empire or Median Kingdom or Kingdom of Media; accept Māda or Mādāya]
swap.clue: Early kings of these people included Deioces and Phraortes.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the last Himyarite king, Abraha's son Ma'd-Karib.
question.text: Ma'd Karib was assisted by this Sassanid shahanshah during a later Axumite invasion of Himyar, which saw this monarch's general Vahrez win the Battle of Hadhramaut. Earlier, he concluded the Eternal Peace with Justinian the Great.
question.clue: This Sasanian emperor who succeeded Kavad I. Most historians believe that Yemen came under Sassanid rule during his reign.

swap.text: Parthian rule ended after this local ruler of Istakhr overthrew Artabanus V and established the Sassanid Empire. This father of Shapur I built a namesake palace as well as the Maiden Castle in the city of Fars, and skirmished with Alexander Severus's forces to the West.
swap.clue: This man, whose early life is the subject of a "book of deeds" or Kar-Namag written in Middle Persian, was the son of a lord of Fars named Papak.
